subject: Cognitive Science
title: Divergent Thinking
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Divergent Thinking.

hook.text: How many uses can you find for a brick? A wall, a weapon, a doorstop, a canvas? That's divergent thinking.

buildup.text: Divergent thinking generates many possible solutions to an open-ended question. Quantity over quality first.

discovery.text: Guilford identified fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration as its core dimensions.

twist.text: Convergent thinking—finding the single right answer—is equally vital. Creativity needs both modes.

climax.text: Brainstorming works only when judgment is suspended. Criticism during idea generation kills divergence.

punchline.text: First generate many ideas. Then pick the best one.

quiz.question: What are the four dimensions of divergent thinking?

details.summary: Divergent thinking generates many possible solutions by exploring multiple directions. Measured by fluency, flexibility, and originality, it contrasts with convergent thinking which finds the single correct answer. Brainstorming and creativity tests rely on divergent thinking ability.
details.whyItMatters: Divergent thinking is the cognitive foundation of creativity. Strengthening it produces more options before convergent thinking selects the best one.
takeaways: Divergent thinking generates multiple possible solutions
It is measured by fluency, flexibility, and originality
Convergent thinking then selects the best from many options

faq.question: How do you measure divergent thinking?
faq.answer: The Alternative Uses Test asks for unusual uses of everyday objects. Scoring counts the number of responses, their variety across categories, and their statistical rarity. More responses, more different categories, and more unusual ideas all indicate stronger divergent thinking ability.

faq.question: Can divergent thinking be improved?
faq.answer: Yes. Practice with open-ended tasks improves fluency. Exposure to diverse experiences increases flexibility. Techniques like random-word association and forced connections train the brain to make unusual links. Quantity-before-quality rules during brainstorming also boost divergent output.
